He wears the scars from wounds delivered by a Pandoran beast across his body like a badge of honor. Biography Beyda’amo has taken a hard line approach with humans. In the past however, he was quite open to human contact, even encouraging his mate, Marali, to attend the school and learn the language of the Sky People. Beyda’amo also received a book from René Harper written by the ancient Chinese general Sun Tzu. However, the so-called "massacre" changed everything. Biography Tan Jala was among the first to reach out to the "Sky People," becoming the de facto tribal ambassador to the humans. He learned English from Dr. René Harper. Soon, the humans’ affronts to the land become impossible for Tan Jala to ignore or excuse. While he understood the frustration of warriors like Beyda'amo and he had been vocal in his anger towards the RDA strip mining, he knew there was still much to be gained by a peaceful bond with the Sky People, and had worked diligently towards it. Tan Jala believes in reaching out with an open hand to the humans rather than striking out with a fist. Peace and harmony are the way of the Na'vi. However, should conflict become unavoidable, Tan Jala is rumored to be one of the Tipani's most lethal and cunning warriors. Tan Jala wears the skin of a viperwolf. text_excerpt: Dr. Jerome 'JJ' Epstein is a member of the Avatar Program and one of the 20 original avatar drivers. Biography Jerome was raised - as many Antarcticans are - with a deep appreciation of environmental preservation. His ecological calling came in the form of an intense lifelong study of the flora and fauna of the distant moon, Pandora. Since arriving as a xenobotanist in the Avatar Program five years ago, he has made great progress as one of the few avatars to find acceptance with the local Na'vi clan, the Tipani. Avatar: The Game Jerome first meets Able Ryder in the Blue Lagoon and requests Ryder collect him some samples of the chalice plant and scorpion thistle. Jerome soon defects with fellow avatars, Dr. René Harper and Dr. Anson Langley. If the player chose to side with the RDA, Ryder is later given an optional mission to kill Jerome due to his betrayal. infobox_fields: species: Na'vi | gender: Female | first: ''Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora'' | portrayed: Kim Nelson
text_excerpt: Ley'taw is a Na'vi in Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora. Background Something of a loner who is friends with Tsu'kiri, Ley'taw prefers to spend time outside the Aranahe Hometree. She's comfortable in her own skin and quick to see the humor in a situation. This leads her to crack jokes, often in a rather blunt manner, and not much surprises her. It's clear that her life in the wild has rubbed the social niceties off her, but no matter how plain-spoken she may be, she is never intentionally cruel. She supports Etuwa as a leader over Ka'nat, unlike her friend Tsu'kiri. A skilled survivalist, she is the clan's lead gatherer and an impressive archer. Gathering in the Kinglor Forest is far from being an easy job, and she cares about the small group under her wing to a fault, ready to do everything to protect them. She cares deeply for her clan and their environment. With the RDA's return, she worries about the forest falling out of balance and wants everything put right again. Avatar: Frontier
